parsedVerdict.reasoning: TaskService is an application-layer use-case service. Its methods (createUser, createProject, createTask, listTasks, markDone) handle use-case orchestration: they validate input, check that referenced entities exist through the TaskRepository interface, create entities with generated IDs and report failures as DomainErrors. The file has no persistence code: it does no storage, SQL or file I/O, and only calls the repository interface. It has no transport logic (no HTTP, request/response or status codes) and no framework code. markDone enforces a state-transition rule ('Task is already done') and mutates task.status directly, and createTask defaults and checks the status. A richer domain model could own these as entity methods. But the application layer coordinating domain rules is within its role, and the rubric's failure cases (persistence, transport or framework logic in the domain, or business rules in infrastructure or presentation) do not apply. No ADR prose was provided.
